title: Fitting ideal sheaf of a finite-type quasi-coherent module
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $r\in\mathbb N$. For each affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$, let $J_U$ be the sum, over all integers $n\geq0$ and all surjective $A$-linear maps $\pi:A^n\to\mathcal F(U)$, of the kernel-minor ideals $I_r(\pi)$ defined in [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] (the unit ideal for $n\leq r$). Define $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)$ to be the largest quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ such that $\mathcal I(U)\subseteq J_U$ for every affine open $U$; concretely it is the sum of all quasi-coherent ideal sheaves satisfying these inclusions. This is a construction of the Fitting ideal sheaf by the affine ideal family: finite generation gives presentations, independence identifies each $J_U$ with every presentation ideal, and localization compatibility identifies this construction with the gluing of those ideals.
